questions.question: What should you do to prevent fatigue while driving?
questions.explanation: A warm, stuffy cab makes you sleepy. Open a window, use a vent, or turn on the air conditioning to keep the cab cool and stay alert.

questions.question: What is true about a distracted driver?

options.text: Is usually aware of what is happening around them.
Is a good person to follow.

questions.explanation: Distracted drivers have slower perception and delayed reaction times. They may make poor decisions. Watch for distracted drivers and stay away from them when possible.

questions.question: How should you hold the steering wheel?

options.text: With one hand, keeping the other hand free for other tasks.
With one hand at a time, alternating between hands.
At the base of the wheel.

questions.explanation: Hold the steering wheel firmly with both hands on opposite sides of the wheel.

questions.question: What will loose belts in an engine compartment cause?

options.text: The water pump and/or fan will not turn properly, causing the engine to overheat.
Make the engine run more efficiently.
Make the fan run too much, causing the engine to run too cold.

questions.correctAnswerText: The water pump and/or fan will not turn properly, causing the engine to overheat.
questions.explanation: Check the tightness of engine belts regularly. Loose belts will not turn the water pump and/or fan properly, which can cause the engine to overheat.

questions.question: What should you do when you leave your vehicle?
questions.explanation: Always apply the parking brake when leaving your vehicle.

questions.question: How often should you check and fill an alcohol evaporator in cold weather?
questions.explanation: An alcohol evaporator prevents ice from building up in the air brake system. In cold weather, check and refill it every day.

questions.question: What happens if air pressure in the air tanks falls below 60 psi?

options.text: A warning light will come on.
The vehicle will not shift out of gear.

questions.correctAnswerText: A warning light will come on.
questions.explanation: When air tank pressure drops below 60 psi, a low pressure warning signal activates. This signal may be a warning light or a wig wag.

questions.question: After changing a tire, what should you do after driving a short distance?

options.text: Check the tightness of the lug nuts.
Ensure that the tire tread depth is good.
Ensure that the correct tire was changed.
See if rocks have gotten into the tread.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check the tightness of the lug nuts.
questions.explanation: After changing a tire, stop a short distance later and re-check that the lug nuts are tight.

questions.question: What is true about a stopped bus?

options.text: Is not a cause for concern.
Is not a concern if passengers are not unloading.
Should not be on the roadway.
Is a concern, whether passengers are visible or not.

questions.correctAnswerText: Is a concern, whether passengers are visible or not.
questions.explanation: Always drive carefully around a stopped bus. Passengers may cross in front of or behind it, and the bus may block their view of your vehicle.

questions.question: During the vehicle inspection test, which of the following will you NOT be required to do?

options.text: Point to or touch each item.
Explain what you are checking and why.

questions.explanation: To earn your CDL, you must pass a vehicle inspection test. You will walk around the vehicle, point to or touch each part, and explain what you are checking and why. You do not need to crawl under the vehicle or engine hood.

questions.question: When a construction worker is near the road, you should:

options.text: Wait until construction is finished before driving.

questions.explanation: In construction zones, follow the posted speed limit. Slow down even more when workers are near the road.

questions.question: When driving a vehicle with a dual brake system, you should:

options.text: Let the vehicle warm up before driving so fuel reaches the engine.
Wait until the air compressor builds 100 psi pressure in both the primary and secondary systems before driving.
Start driving right after the vehicle starts.
Pump the pedal 20 times to build pressure, then drive.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait until the air compressor builds 100 psi pressure in both the primary and secondary systems before driving.
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with a dual air system, let the air compressor build at least 100 psi pressure in both the primary and secondary systems.

questions.question: The parking brake should be:

options.text: Used every time you park the vehicle.
Set when driving in bad weather.
Used to stop the vehicle during normal driving.

questions.correctAnswerText: Used every time you park the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Always use the parking brake when you park your vehicle.

questions.question: If an aggressive driver confronts you, you should:

options.text: Make eye contact with the driver.
Challenge the driver to a race.

questions.explanation: When you meet an aggressive driver, get away from them if you can. Do not make eye contact, challenge them, or respond to rude gestures.

questions.question: What does ABS do?

options.text: Prevent the wheels from locking up.
Prevent the air compressor from overheating.
Prevent front brakes from being used on ice.
Prevent brakes from being used if downshifting is better.

questions.correctAnswerText: Prevent the wheels from locking up.
questions.explanation: Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) stops the wheels from locking up when you brake hard, especially on slippery surfaces.

questions.question: When driving long distances, you should take a break every ____ to avoid fatigue.
questions.explanation: Stop for a break at least every two hours or every 100 miles to prevent fatigue on long trips.

questions.question: The suspension system:

options.text: Supports the vehicle and its cargo.
Keeps cargo at the correct distance from the driver.
Reduces the load on the tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: Supports the vehicle and its cargo.
questions.explanation: The suspension system holds up the vehicle and its cargo while keeping the axles in position. A damaged suspension system is dangerous.

questions.question: If the brakes pull to one side when you use them, it means:

options.text: The brakes need to be serviced.
The brakes have too much power.

questions.correctAnswerText: The brakes need to be serviced.
questions.explanation: If your vehicle pulls to one side when braking, you have a brake problem. Fix it before driving. Driving an unsafe vehicle breaks federal and state laws.

questions.question: Sending text messages while driving:

options.text: Is okay if the messages are short.
Is allowed if you are asking your employer a question.

questions.explanation: You cannot send or read text messages while driving.

questions.question: Cargo on flatbed trailers must be:
questions.explanation: Tie down all cargo on flatbed trailers to prevent it from shifting or falling during transport.

questions.question: What should you do before entering a curve?
questions.explanation: Always shift to a lower gear before entering a curve. Slowing down before the curve helps you control your vehicle better while turning.

questions.question: When traveling across state lines, how many driver licenses should you have?

options.text: One license for each state you visit.
One license for each state where you plan to stop.
One license for your starting state and one for your ending state.

questions.explanation: You cannot have more than one driver license. All states share driver information in a database to prevent people from getting multiple licenses.

questions.question: What may be in the air that enters air storage tanks?
questions.explanation: Air that enters air storage tanks usually contains water and compressor oil. Tanks have drains to remove these materials so they don't damage the brake system.

questions.question: When backing up, should you use a helper?

options.text: No, they often add to the confusion.
Only if you don't feel confident.
No, they get in the way.

questions.explanation: Backing up is always dangerous because you cannot see everything behind your vehicle. Use a helper whenever you can to watch your blind spots.

questions.question: What is hydroplaning?

options.text: When tires lose grip on the road.
When tires grip the road better.
When front tires grip better than rear tires.
When front tires grip less than rear tires.

questions.correctAnswerText: When tires lose grip on the road.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens on wet roads when tires lose grip and slide on a layer of water.

questions.question: Before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes, what minimum pressure should build up in both systems?
questions.explanation: Before driving a vehicle with dual air brakes, let the air compressor build up at least 100 psi in both the primary and secondary systems.

questions.question: What does the ABS warning light mean when it comes on while driving?

options.text: The ABS is not working correctly.
The ABS needs to be turned on.

questions.correctAnswerText: The ABS is not working correctly.
questions.explanation: Vehicles with ABS have yellow warning lights. When these lights come on, there is a problem with the brake system. You may have lost ABS on one or more wheels.

questions.question: When using spring brakes with a heavy load, how long will it take to stop?
questions.explanation: Spring brakes activate when air pressure gets too low. A heavily loaded vehicle takes a long time to stop using only spring brakes because they don't work on all axles.

questions.question: What should you NOT do when using a turn signal?

options.text: Turn off the signal after completing the turn.
Leave the signal on long after the turn is done.

questions.correctAnswerText: Leave the signal on long after the turn is done.
questions.explanation: Signal well before you turn or change lanes. Keep the signal on until you finish the turn, then turn it off so other drivers don't get confused.

questions.question: What is an advantage of convex mirrors?

options.text: They cannot be used on vehicles with hazardous materials.
They help a driver see a large area.
They are legal in all states.

questions.correctAnswerText: They help a driver see a large area.
questions.explanation: Convex mirrors are curved to give drivers a wider view than flat mirrors. However, objects in convex mirrors look smaller and farther away than they really are.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a serious traffic violation?

options.text: Not stopping behind the stop line at a stop sign.

questions.correctAnswerText: Not stopping behind the stop line at a stop sign.
questions.explanation: Serious traffic violations include speeding, reckless driving, driving a truck without a valid license, following too closely, and improper lane usage. Multiple serious violations can result in losing your license.

questions.question: When carrying 30 feet of cargo on a flatbed trailer, what is the minimum number of tie-downs needed?
questions.explanation: Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. All cargo must have at least two tie-downs, no matter how small.

questions.question: Which activity does NOT cause a distraction while driving?
questions.explanation: Anything that takes your attention away from driving is a dangerous distraction. This includes eating, drinking, smoking, and adjusting the radio or climate controls.

questions.question: What does an Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) do?
questions.explanation: An Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) prevents wheel lockup during hard braking. It gives you better control of the vehicle, but it does not necessarily make the vehicle stop faster.

questions.question: What should you check on power steering hoses?

options.text: To ensure that they are still clear.
To ensure that they are connected to the battery.
For the proper amount of brake fluid.

questions.explanation: When checking power steering hoses, pumps, and fluid level, look for leaks in the hoses.

questions.question: What is the minimum number of tie-downs required to secure cargo on a flatbed trailer?
questions.explanation: Use at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. All cargo must have at least two tie-downs, no matter how small.

questions.question: When turning to avoid a hazard, what should you do?

options.text: You should not brake as it could cause the wheels to lock.
You should turn the wheel very sharply.
You should hold down the brakes until you are past the hazard.

questions.correctAnswerText: You should not brake as it could cause the wheels to lock.
questions.explanation: Do not brake while turning to avoid a hazard. Braking while turning can lock the wheels and cause a skid.

questions.question: When you start a vehicle, what should happen to the warning lights and buzzers?

options.text: Should stay on for several minutes.
Should turn off within a few seconds.
Should stay on until manually turned off.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should turn off within a few seconds.
questions.explanation: After the engine starts, warning lights and buzzers for oil, coolant, charging circuits, and the Anti-Lock Braking System (ABS) should turn off right away.

questions.question: When should you use high beam headlights?

options.text: Are not usually necessary when driving at night.
Provide better light than the sun.
Should be on the high beam setting whenever possible.
Should always be on the high beam setting.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be on the high beam setting whenever possible.
questions.explanation: Use high beam headlights at night when it is safe and legal to improve visibility. However, dim your lights to low beam within 500 feet of an approaching vehicle so you do not blind other drivers.

questions.question: How much water is needed on a road for a vehicle to hydroplane?

options.text: A significant amount, such as a large puddle

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when a vehicle's tires lose grip on the road and glide on water. Only a small amount of water on the road is needed for this to happen.

questions.question: What is brake lag?

options.text: The delay between pushing the brake pedal and the brakes starting to work
The distance between where the brake pedal rests and the floor
The amount of air pressure needed to stop a vehicle
How worn down the brakes are

questions.correctAnswerText: The delay between pushing the brake pedal and the brakes starting to work
questions.explanation: Air brakes have a delay because air must travel through air lines to reach the brakes. This delay is called brake lag and usually lasts at least half a second. Hydraulic brakes work right away when you press the pedal.

questions.question: During exercises other than straight line backing, how many times can you exit your vehicle to check its position?
questions.explanation: You can exit your vehicle to check its position during basic control skills tests. This is called a "look." For straight line backing, you can look only once. For other exercises, you can look up to two times.

questions.question: How many red reflective warning triangles should you place when your vehicle is stopped on the road?
questions.explanation: Place three red reflective triangles as warning devices when your vehicle is parked on the road.

questions.question: Before starting down a hill, you should:
questions.explanation: Always shift to a low gear before going downhill. Gravity will cause your vehicle to speed up as you go down, so low gear helps control your speed.

questions.question: What is the purpose of a vehicle inspection report?

options.text: To tell the motor carrier about problems that need to be fixed
To make sure the vehicle is inspected on schedule
To hold drivers accountable for inspecting their vehicles
To plan the next five trips

questions.correctAnswerText: To tell the motor carrier about problems that need to be fixed
questions.explanation: A vehicle inspection report lets you tell the motor carrier about safety issues with the vehicle. Complete one after each day of driving. Write down any problems that could affect safe operation or cause a breakdown.

questions.question: How can you warn drivers behind you when you need to brake?

options.text: Lightly tap your brakes a few times
Stick your arm out the window

questions.correctAnswerText: Lightly tap your brakes a few times
questions.explanation: Lightly tap your brake pedal a few times to make your brake lights flash. This warns drivers behind you that you are slowing down.

questions.question: On a truck with air brakes, what does the air compressor do?

options.text: Pumps air into the air storage tanks
Moves air to the back of the truck

questions.correctAnswerText: Pumps air into the air storage tanks
questions.explanation: The air compressor pumps air into the air storage tanks. The air compressor governor controls it.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a distracted person that drivers should worry about?

options.text: A driver talking to another person in the vehicle
Children on the side of the road
Construction workers on the side of the road
A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus

questions.correctAnswerText: A person sitting on a bench waiting for a bus
questions.explanation: Drivers talking to passengers may not pay full attention to the road. Children do not always watch for traffic and may run into the street. Be careful near road workers. A person waiting on a bench for a bus is not a distraction concern.

questions.question: If you drive a truck that requires a CDL, what is the seat belt requirement?

options.text: You do not need to wear a seat belt
You must wear a seat belt only if carrying more than 500 pounds of cargo
You must always wear a seat belt
You must wear a seat belt only when driving a tank trailer

questions.correctAnswerText: You must always wear a seat belt
questions.explanation: For safety, you must wear your seat belt at all times while operating a truck that requires a CDL.

questions.question: If you feel tired before a drive, what should you do?

options.text: Drive as fast as possible to get there quickly

questions.explanation: Caffeine and other stimulants may keep you awake, but they will not make you more alert. Tiredness means your body needs sleep. The only real solution is to stop driving and get sleep.
